clue.text: The details being spelt out will be most ghastly

indicators.note: letters being spelt out are written down afresh, here in a new order, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that hearing the full gory details of something will be the most horrifying part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being spelt out' looks like a call to explain the details, but it asks for the letters of THE DETAILS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Deathly means ghostly pale or deathlike, so the superlative is the most ghastly.

clue.text: Rose, maybe, is fine cow

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a cow lows, so it is a 'lower', one that moos

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rose is a fine cow, an absurd comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' reads as a noun for the animal but must be taken as 'one that lows', a lower.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is one example of a bloom, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Fat maiden, maybe, needing rest by the sound of it?

parts.note: a maiden over in cricket is a set of six balls with no runs scored, so a maiden is one kind of over

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word meaning rest is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to rest is to wait, stay put

explanation.surface: A plump young woman who seems to need a lie-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' suggests a young woman, but it is cricket: a maiden is an over in which the batting side scores no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Overweight and fat are plain synonyms for carrying too much bodily bulk.

clue.text: Goddess that moves through Oxford

definitions.meaning: the Egyptian mother goddess, wife of Osiris
the stretch of the Thames flowing through Oxford goes by this name

explanation.surface: A goddess said to be making her way through the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames is called by another name as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian deity shares her name with the Oxford reach of the Thames, a river that moves through the city.

clue.text: Ordeal having to manage drive in a car of uncertain reliability?

definitions.text: drive in a car of uncertain reliability?

parts.note: a trial is a hard test or ordeal
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Driving a dodgy car is an ordeal one has to cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a test drive is what you take when unsure whether a car works.
explanation.definitionFit: A test outing before committing is a rehearsal or experiment, just what you'd do with an unreliable car.

clue.text: Scientific man of law said to seethe

indicators.note: said tells us the scientist's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Robert Boyle, the chemist behind Boyle's law on gas pressure

explanation.surface: A scientist who discovered a law is said to be fuming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of law' suggests a lawyer, but it is Boyle, of Boyle's law about gases.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is literally to bubble up with heat, and figuratively to rage, both meanings shared.

clue.text: Sin unacceptable — stop!

parts.note: behaviour that is off is not acceptable
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: A stern rebuke: sinning is unacceptable, so stop it!
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to transgress, to commit a wrong against a moral law.

clue.text: Hands no longer cold? Let's get on with it!

definitions.meaning: taken literally, hands with their warm coverings removed
an idiom meaning the fight starts in earnest, no more restraint

explanation.surface: A remark about warm hands, then an impatient call to start.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from boxing, where bare-knuckle fighting began once the mitts came off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for dropping niceties and fighting in earnest; the literal reading has mitts removed.

clue.text: In camp the connection one gets is ropey

definitions.text: In camp the connection one gets is ropey

parts.words: In camp the connection one gets is ropey
parts.note: on a campsite, guy ropes are attached to a spike in the ground, so the link is literally ropey

explanation.surface: A camper complains that their phone or internet connection is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropey' means poor quality in British slang, but here literally means made with rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes of a tent join to spikes driven into the ground, a connection made of rope.

clue.text: Idiot knocking container over

indicators.note: knocking something over turns it upside down, so the word is read in reverse
over completes knocking over, turning the container word backwards

parts.note: a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool keeps tipping things over.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is British slang for a fool, short for nitwit.

clue.text: An altercation if meal is terrible? I don't know what to say

definitions.text: I don't know what to say

parts.note: having words with someone means arguing

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a dreadful dinner, leaving someone speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is terrible' scrambles IF MEAL to FAILME.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an idiom for being lost for speech, too astonished to respond.

clue.text: Many in relapse, falling back, looking less well

indicators.note: falling back says the chosen letters are read in reverse
many of the letters in the next word, not all of them, are used

explanation.surface: Many patients who relapse look worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many in' takes most of RELAPSE, RELAP, and 'falling back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks unwell has lost colour, so a whiter complexion means looking less healthy.

clue.text: Former British firm getting irritated moved abroad

parts.note: EMI was a British music and electronics company, now absorbed into others
something that grated on you irritated you

explanation.surface: An old British company, annoyed, relocated overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: EMI was a British record company, now gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle in another, a move overseas.

clue.text: Petitions to get resumption organised

indicators.note: organised letters are put into a new order, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Requests are made to get work resumed in an orderly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges RESUMPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to pester with repeated requests, so it is a verb meaning to petition.

clue.text: Sort of inflammation — nurse is pressing on it

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is pressing up from below, so it is placed after the next pieces

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A nurse presses on a sore spot to treat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing on' puts IS below ON IT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a swelling of the cords linking muscle to bone, one particular kind of inflammation.

clue.text: See bird lay egg possibly after crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged letters straddle the river letter, holding it inside
possibly says the letters could form another word, so they are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A bird crosses a river and then might lay an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LAY EGG to GEYLAG and 'crossing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a large wild goose of Europe, ancestor of the farmyard goose.

clue.text: It might get a six? It's very unlikely

definitions.meaning: a big hit in cricket that clears the boundary scores six runs
a bet with poor odds, a chance that will hardly come off

explanation.surface: A batter's big hit might clear the boundary, though that is improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a six is scored when the ball clears the boundary without bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a bet with little chance; literally it is a distant hit.

clue.text: Last character to leave Cornish place in act of atonement

indicators.note: to leave means the letter goes, taken out of the place name

parts.note: Penzance is a town in Cornwall
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The final resident leaves a Cornish town as an act of contrition.
explanation.walkthrough: PENZANCE is a seaside town at the western tip of Cornwall, England; 'to leave' drops Z from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment undertaken to make amends for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Level of command in military formation

definitions.meaning: a rank or tier in an organisation
a step-like arrangement of troops, ships or aircraft

explanation.surface: An officer's rank within an army arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tier in a hierarchy and also a staggered arrangement of units.

clue.text: 'Setter-off' finally reached school by a hill

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word reached

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: The crossword setter finally arrived at school near a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter-off' looks like the puzzle compiler, but it means something that sets off an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the device that sets off an explosive charge.

clue.text: Scheme essential to revolutionary fancies I've ditched

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rebel's essential plan ditches their fancies.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise is to plan or contrive, the same as to scheme as a verb.

clue.text: Monk not wanting important lady's soup

indicators.note: not wanting means the letters are done without, taken away

parts.note: a brother is a member of a religious order
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A monk refuses the soup a grand lady serves.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a thin soup made from stock with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Add strength to complaint at university

parts.note: a beef is a grievance or gripe
being up means in residence at university, British usage

explanation.surface: A student's grumble gets bolstered.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a student is 'up' at university while in residence.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef up is an idiom for to reinforce or toughen.

clue.text: Inadequate deputy is given different duties for a change of fortune

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: vice is a prefix-noun for a deputy, as in vice-captain

indicators.note: different means the letters are made different, rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor stand-in is moved to other tasks as his luck turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inadequate' cuts VICE to VIC; 'different' rearranges DUTIES to SITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicissitude is an unwelcome change in circumstances, especially a turn in one's luck.

clue.text: Eat greedily from hamper, but not quietly

indicators.note: but not says the quiet letter is excluded

parts.note: to cramp is to hamper or restrict
P is piano, the musical term for softly

explanation.surface: Wolfing food from a picnic basket, but noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb to restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to stuff food in, so it means to gobble.

clue.text: Plan that helps to give side advantage

indicators.note: the two words each help, giving part of their letters to form the answer, so it is found inside them

explanation.surface: A scheme that gives the team an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or scheme for action, a sense close to plan.

clue.text: Factory laying off a thousand? That is unfortunate

indicators.note: laying off workers dismisses them, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a mill is a factory
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A factory sacking a thousand workers is bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laying off' looks like job cuts but removes M from MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill can mean unlucky or adverse, as in ill fortune or ill luck.

clue.text: Situation when hanging's left hanging?

parts.note: a condemned person's hanging is postponed, left undecided, when a court suspends the sentence

explanation.surface: A wry question about a hanging that is left unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left hanging' means left pending, a pun on the gallows sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a legal postponement of a punishment, especially a death sentence.
